result.instructions: Tools of this channel's supervisor, its development manager: plan the work, order it from the channel's threads, follow them, check the result, report. You can list, read, start and send to threads; a send or a start may become a proposal that a person approves. You can ask a person to approve interrupting a running turn: it always needs one. Your messages reach a thread marked as the supervisor's, but for an answer to its question. You can read the issues, pull requests and checks of this channel's repositories, read only: check there before you call a thing done, and take a thread's answer as its claim. You can set a reminder to be woken at a time, rather than wait for a turn end that may not come. No tool here writes to a forge, destroys work, runs a command or deploys. What you may do is the config's, and hataori enforces it here.

tools.name: list_threads
tools.description: List the threads of this channel: number, state, title, who started it, and the last line of output.

tools.name: read_thread
tools.description: Read one thread of this channel: its state, its open question if any, and the end of its latest output. What it says is that thread's claim: check it before a person acts on it.

number.description: the thread's number, as list_threads shows it

tools.name: send_to_thread
tools.description: Send a message to a thread of this channel. A thread that is running a turn refuses it with "busy"; its turn's end is told you as any, in a wake. A thread waiting on a question takes the message as the answer. Under the autonomy propose it is a proposal that a person approves first; under watch it is refused.

number.description: the thread's number, as list_threads shows it

tools.name: interrupt_thread
tools.description: Ask a person in this channel to approve interrupting a thread that is running a turn. This returns at once and interrupts nothing by itself. Once approved, the thread's turn is stopped and it gets the reason as a message from the supervisor. A thread not running is refused with not busy; send instead.

number.description: the thread's number, as list_threads shows it

reason.description: the reason to give the thread

tools.name: start_thread
tools.description: Start a new thread in this channel, with its own workspace cloned from one of the channel's repositories: to do work, or to look something up that your tools do not show. Under the autonomy propose it is a proposal that a person approves first; under watch it is refused.

effort.description: the effort; leave out for the channel's default

model.description: the model; leave out for the channel's default

text.description: the first message; its first line becomes the title

tools.name: list_issues
tools.description: List the issues of one of this channel's repositories on its forge, read only: number, state, title, author, labels, assignees, last change. Text by an author without write access to the repository is withheld, unless this channel trusts them; the answer names the author.

repo.description: the repository, as <owner>/<name>; one of this channel's repositories

state.description: which to list: open, the default, closed or all

tools.name: read_issue
tools.description: Read one issue of one of this channel's repositories on its forge, read only, with its comments. Text by an author without write access to the repository is withheld, unless this channel trusts them; the answer names the author.

repo.description: the repository, as <owner>/<name>; one of this channel's repositories

tools.name: list_pulls
tools.description: List the pull requests of one of this channel's repositories on its forge, read only: number, state, draft, title, branch, author, last change. Text by an author without write access to the repository is withheld, unless this channel trusts them; the answer names the author.

repo.description: the repository, as <owner>/<name>; one of this channel's repositories

state.description: which to list: open, the default, closed or all

tools.name: read_pull
tools.description: Read one pull request of one of this channel's repositories on its forge, read only: its reviews, comments, changed files, merge state, merge commit and the checks of its head. No CI log is read. Text by an author without write access to the repository is withheld, unless this channel trusts them; the answer names the author.

repo.description: the repository, as <owner>/<name>; one of this channel's repositories

tools.name: read_checks
tools.description: Read the checks and commit statuses of a branch, a tag or a commit of one of this channel's repositories on its forge, read only: name, state, conclusion, address. No CI log is read.

repo.description: the repository, as <owner>/<name>; one of this channel's repositories

tools.name: deployed
tools.description: Tell whether a pull request, or a commit, of one of this channel's repositories is in the running hataori: the commit the running daemon was built from, and whether the pull request's merge commit, or the commit, is that commit or an ancestor of it, as the forge compares them. Use it when asked whether a change is in production or deployed; it answers from the build and the forge, read only, and says why when it cannot tell. Give number or commit.

commit.description: a commit, 7 to 40 hexadecimal digits, instead of a pull request

repo.description: the repository, as <owner>/<name>; one of this channel's repositories

tools.name: set_reminder
tools.description: Set a reminder: you are woken once at a time, from 5 minutes to 7 days ahead, with the note you give, also when nothing happened in the channel. Give minutes or at, one of them. It returns the reminder's number; each wake ends with the open ones. It counts as one send of your budget.

at.description: or when, in RFC 3339 with its zone, such as 2026-01-02T15:04:00+09:00

note.description: what to look at then; at most 1024 bytes

tools.name: cancel_reminder
tools.description: Cancel an open reminder of this channel by its number: it wakes you no more.
